value: some behavioural sensitivity to ultraviolet light, in forced-choice lit-versus-unlit LED discrimination tests with 7 deer
method: automated forced-choice discrimination of lit from unlit monochromatic LED lights, intensity lowered until the deer could no longer discriminate; logistic function fitted per deer to give a threshold at each wavelength
conditions: 7 deer; light-adapted; the abstract gives no wavelengths, intensities, ages, sexes or whether deer were captive; thresholds at the short and long ends of the purported visual spectrum were compared

source.authors: Cohen BS, Osborn DA, Gallagher GR, Warren RJ, Miller KV
source.title: Behavioral measure of the light-adapted visual sensitivity of white-tailed deer

value: of five insecticidal lamps, the one peaking at 363 nm was most effective for male trapping; males were caught at all five lamps and female captures were minimal
method: field light-trapping with five insecticidal lamps (L360, L365, L370, L380, L405) run side by side
conditions: Pingtan County, Fuzhou, Fujian, China; wavelength tests 26-28 June and 3-5 July 2018 and 4-6 June 2019; lamps hung at 2 m, about 50 m apart and randomly placed daily, on from 19:00 to 04:00; peak-emergence catch 2,902 males and 9 females in total (female:male 1:322); the page text read does not map the L-labels to peak wavelengths other than 363 nm for the most effective lamp, and gives no replicate count; lamp spectra differ in more than peak wavelength, so this is a catch comparison, not a spectral sensitivity

method: indoor phototaxis tests with moths held in net cages 7.0 m from a 25 W L360 lamp in a darkened room
conditions: tests 28-31 May 2021; Test 1 used 44 males and 43 females, Test 2 used 89 males and 78 females, Test 3 used 30 egg-laying females and none responded (Results 3.4); the Results give 14.6% as an average response rate of non-ovipositing females; the sentences read do not say how many females the 14.6% rests on or how the tests were pooled; male rates are not quoted here
